Especially, for the T300 Al2618 alloy, a couple of large-sized dimples appear on the fracture surface, as observed in Fig. 10c. Such large dimples suggest the occurrence of grain boundary sliding [39].
The introduction of TiB2 particles on one hand refined the grain size, providing grain refinement accordingly.
TiB2 particles provide load bearing strengthening effect by transferring loading from Al matrix, which enhances the yield strength of the composite.
In addition, the submicron-sized TiB2 particles can act as obstacles to inhibit the dislocation migration via the Orowan effect and result in an increase of YS.
Owing to the mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients between TiB2 and Al matrix, the dislocation density in the matrix is increased, leading to the strengthening of the composite.
In the subsequent thermal exposure, the growth of the fine grains is limited by the TiB2 particle bands.

It is suggested that at 300 °C (~ 0.6 Tm of Al), thermal activated dislocation climbing and cross-slipping becomes severe during deformation, which can weaken the grain size strengthening effect by releasing the dislocations pile-ups at grain boundaries [64].

The CTE mismatch strengthening makes a major contributions to YS by enhancing the dislocation density in Al matrix at RT and elevated temperatures, while the other mechanisms play a minor role in strengthening.
Compared to the Al2618 matrix alloy, the TiB2/Al2618 composite furtherly enhances the room and high temperature strength, and also improves the strength retention after thermal exposure.
